description:
crl.rs:258 and ocsp.rs:363 use .map_err(|_| Error::CrlSignatureInvalid) and .map_err(|_| Error::OcspSignatureInvalid), dropping the underlying signature::Error entirely.

The signature::Error may carry a meaningful source() chain (algorithm mismatch, malformed key, wrong curve, etc.). Silently replacing it with a unit variant means:
- Callers can't distinguish 'wrong algorithm OID' from 'bit-flip in signature bytes' from 'malformed SPKI'.
- Debugging certificate mis-issuance or interop failures requires guesswork rather than following the error chain.

Fix options:
1. Add a wrapping variant: CrlSignatureInvalid(signature::Error) (breaking change, but gives full context).
2. Wrap as CrlParseError(der::Error) with a synthetic der::Error (lossy but preserves the chain shape).
3. Add a non_exhaustive CrlSignatureError { detail: String } variant that captures the Display of the inner error without requiring signature crate in public API.

References: R2 (map_err discarding error context)
title: rusty: map_err(|_|) discards verifier error on CRL/OCSP signature failure
